intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from local street vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a budget walking food tour or explore independently for an authentic culinary adventure.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An on foot, visiting centuries-old merchant houses, tailor shops, and temples. On the 14th of each lunar month, the town turns off electric lights and glows with hundreds of colorful silk lanterns reflected in the Thu Bon River — a magical and deeply cultural experience.

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Backpacker Boat Tour
experiences.description: Take a budget day trip from Ho Chi Minh City into the Mekong Delta, navigating narrow canals by sampan boat, visiting floating markets, coconut candy workshops, and rice paper factories. Interact with local farmers and taste fresh tropical fruits straight from the orchards.

experiences.name: Hue Imperial Citadel and Royal Tomb Cycling
experiences.description: Rent a bicycle and spend a day exploring the historic Imperial Citadel of the Nguyen Dynasty, then cycle out to the ornate royal tombs of Emperor Tu Duc and Minh Mang set among pine forests and lotus ponds. Stop at local com hen (clam rice) stalls along the Perfume River for an authentic Hue culinary experience.

experiences.name: Bui Vien Walking Street Night Experience
experiences.description: Dive into the heart of Ho Chi Minh City's backpacker scene on Bui Vien Street, where budget bars, street food stalls, and live music create a vibrant atmosphere. Sample banh trang nuong (Vietnamese pizza), fresh spring rolls, and bia hoi (draft beer) while mingling with fellow travelers and locals in one of Southeast Asia's most energetic nightlife strips.
experiences.location: Pham Ngu Lao Backpacker District, Ho Chi Minh City

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly public bus No. 86 (45,000 VND) or negotiate a shared taxi to the Old Quarter. Check into Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk through the winding streets of the Old Quarter to get your bearings. Explore Hang Gai, Hang Bac, and Hang Dao streets.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hoan Kiem Lake for a relaxing evening stroll. Watch locals doing tai chi and socializing around the lake. Cross the red Huc Bridge to visit Ngoc Son Temple (30,000 VND entrance). Then dive into your first taste of Hanoi street food on Ta Hien Street (Beer Street).

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a Banh Mi sandwich from a street vendor near the Old Quarter for around 25,000-35,000 VND
meals.dinner: Bun Cha (grilled pork with noodles) at a local street stall on Hang Manh Street for 50,000-70,000 VND. Pair with a Bia Hoi (fresh draught beer) for just 10,000-15,000 VND on Ta Hien Street

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a local bank/gold shop in the Old Quarter for better rates. Avoid airport taxi touts. Keep your valuables secure in the busy Old Quarter. Budget tip: Bus No. 86 from airport costs only 45,000 VND vs 300,000+ VND for private taxi.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and head to a local pho stall for a traditional Vietnamese breakfast. Walk to Hoan Kiem Lake for the morning atmosphere. Visit the Ngoc Son Temple if you missed it last night. Stroll through the Old Quarter's 36 ancient guild streets, each named after the trade once practiced there (Hang Bac - Silver Street, Hang Gai - Silk Street, etc.).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (free, but check opening hours - closed Mon & Fri afternoons). Explore the One Pillar Pagoda (free) and Ho Chi Minh Museum (40,000 VND). Walk through the Ba Dinh Square area. Head to the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) - Vietnam's first university, entrance 30,000 VND.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter and explore the vibrant night market on Hang Dao Street (open Fri-Sun) or wander through the food stalls. Try street food snacks as you walk. End the evening at a Bia Hoi corner for cheap local beer.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) at a local street stall near the hotel - 40,000-60,000 VND
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodle salad) at a local restaurant near Temple of Literature - 50,000-70,000 VND
meals.dinner: Nem Cuon (fresh spring rolls) and Cha Ca La Vong (turmeric fish) at a budget local restaurant on Cha Ca Street - 80,000-120,000 VND total

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum requires conservative dress (covered shoulders and knees). It is closed on Mondays and Fridays and for maintenance from September to November. Arrive early to avoid queues. Total estimated spend today: 200,000-300,000 VND (~$8-12 USD).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dong Xuan Market - Hanoi's largest covered market - early morning when it's most lively. Browse fresh produce, street food, and local goods on the ground floor. Great for people-watching and photography. Walk through the surrounding streets filled with wholesale vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (66,000 VND) - one of Southeast Asia's best museums showcasing Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups with outdoor traditional houses. Take bus No. 14 from the Old Quarter (9,000 VND). Spend 2-3 hours exploring the fascinating exhibits and outdoor village reconstructions.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the Old Quarter and join a free walking tour led by local university students (tip-based, 50,000-100,000 VND suggested). These 'Hanoi Free Walking Tours' depart from Hoan Kiem Lake area. Afterward, explore the vibrant street food scene on Ly Quoc Su Street.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street vendor near Dong Xuan Market - 20,000-30,000 VND
meals.lunch: Bun Rieu (crab and tomato noodle soup) from a street stall near the museum - 40,000-60,000 VND
meals.dinner: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) and assorted street snacks on Ly Quoc Su Street - 60,000-80,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: The Vietnam Museum of Ethnology is closed on Mondays. The free walking tours are an excellent way to learn about local history and culture while supporting student guides. Budget tip: use local buses throughout Hanoi for 9,000 VND per ride instead of taxis.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 - April 18, 2027 (Day Trip to Ninh Binh)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat bus station to Ninh Binh (around 80,000-100,000 VND, 2 hours). Arrive and rent a bicycle (50,000-80,000 VND/day) to explore the area. Cycle to Trang An Landscape Complex - a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Take a boat tour through the stunning limestone karst caves and rice paddies (250,000 VND for a 2-3 hour boat trip).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to Bich Dong Pagoda (free) - a beautiful pagoda built into a limestone cliff with three levels to explore. Continue to Tam Coc area for more scenic views of the 'Halong Bay on land' landscape. Climb up to Mua Cave viewpoint (100,000 VND) for panoramic views over the rice fields and karst mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ninh Binh town, enjoy a local dinner, then take a late afternoon/evening bus back to Hanoi (last bus around 18:00-19:00). Return to your hotel in the Old Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Grab a Banh Mi or sticky rice before catching the bus - 25,000-35,000 VND
meals.lunch: Com Nieu (clay pot rice) - a Ninh Binh specialty - at a local restaurant near Tam Coc - 60,000-80,000 VND
meals.dinner: De Nuong (grilled goat meat) - another Ninh Binh specialty - at a local restaurant before heading back - 80,000-120,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Start very early (6:00-7:00 AM) to maximize your time in Ninh Binh. Alternatively, consider staying overnight in Ninh Binh for a more relaxed experience. Wear comfortable shoes for cycling. Bring sunscreen and water. Total day trip budget approximately 600,000-800,000 VND (~$25-33 USD) including transport.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Hanoi hotel. Take a grab bike or walk to Hanoi train station. Board the Reunification Express train to Hue (SE trains, around 300,000-500,000 VND for a hard seat or soft seat - book in advance). The journey takes approximately 13-14 hours but the scenery is spectacular. Settle in and enjoy the passing Vietnamese countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your train journey southward. The train passes through beautiful coastal scenery and rice paddies. Chat with fellow travelers and locals on the train. Bring snacks and water for the journey. The train passes through the stunning Hai Van Pass section after Da Nang.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Hue in the late evening (around 22:00-23:00 depending on the train). Check into a budget guesthouse in the city center near the Citadel area (dorm beds from 100,000-150,000 VND, private rooms from 200,000-350,000 VND). Get a quick late-night snack and rest.

meals.breakfast: Pho or Banh Mi near Hanoi train station before departure - 40,000-60,000 VND
meals.lunch: Train snacks and food vendors who board at stations - 30,000-50,000 VND. Alternatively bring your own food.
meals.dinner: Quick bowl of Bun Bo Hue (Hue-style spicy beef noodle soup) from a late-night stall near your guesthouse - 40,000-60,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets in advance through the Vietnam Railways website (dsvn.vn) or at the station. The overnight/long train journey is a classic backpacker experience in Vietnam. Bring a light jacket as train AC can be cold. Consider a soft seat for more comfort on this long journey. Budget tip: the train is much more scenic and culturally immersive than flying.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head to the Imperial Citadel of Hue (Imperial City) - a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The entrance fee is 200,000 VND and covers the main citadel complex. Spend 2-3 hours exploring the Forbidden Purple City, Thai Hoa Palace, and the beautiful gates and towers. Hire an audio guide for deeper context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (50,000-80,000 VND/day) and cycle along the Perfume River to visit the Royal Tombs. The Tomb of Tu Duc (100,000 VND) is the most elaborate and picturesque. Also visit Thien Mu Pagoda (free) - Hue's iconic seven-story pagoda overlooking the river. The cycling route along the river is beautiful and very budget-friendly.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hue's famous street food scene. Walk along Le Loi Street and the area around Dong Ba Market for evening street food. Try multiple small dishes - Hue cuisine is considered one of Vietnam's finest regional cuisines.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Hue or Com Hen (rice with baby mussels) - a Hue breakfast specialty - 30,000-50,000 VND
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Hue (spicy lemongrass beef noodle soup) at a local restaurant - 40,000-60,000 VND. This is the dish's hometown!
meals.dinner: Hue street food feast: Banh Khoai (crispy pancakes), Nem Lui (lemongrass skewers), and Banh Beo (steamed rice cakes) - 80,000-120,000 VND total at street stalls near Dong Ba Market

day_by_day.notes: Hue is famous for its royal cuisine and street food - don't miss the opportunity to try as many local specialties as possible. The city is compact and very bikeable. Dress modestly when visiting temples and pagodas. Budget estimate for the day: 500,000-700,000 VND (~$20-28 USD).

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Hue guesthouse. Take a budget minibus or open tour bus to Hoi An via the Hai Van Pass (around 100,000-150,000 VND, 3-4 hours). The route over the Hai Van Pass offers some of Vietnam's most dramatic coastal scenery. Stop at the summit for photos overlooking Da Nang Bay. Optionally stop briefly in Da Nang.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hoi An and check into a budget guesthouse in or near the Ancient Town (dorm beds from 100,000-150,000 VND). Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town on foot - it's compact and very walkable. Visit the Japanese Covered Bridge (free to view from outside, 120,000 VND for the combined Ancient Town ticket to enter). Wander through the colorful lantern-lit streets.
day_by_day.evening: The Ancient Town truly comes alive at night with thousands of colorful silk lanterns illuminating the streets. Walk along the Thu Bon River, browse the night market, and soak in the magical atmosphere. Buy a small floating lantern (10,000-15,000 VND) to release on the river for good luck.

meals.breakfast: Quick Banh Mi or pho before departure from Hue - 30,000-50,000 VND
meals.lunch: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish) at a local restaurant in the Ancient Town - 50,000-70,000 VND
meals.dinner: White Rose dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) and Com Ga Hoi An (Hoi An chicken rice) at street stalls near the central market - 60,000-90,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: The Ancient Town entrance ticket (120,000 VND) is required to enter most historic buildings and is valid for multiple sites. You can walk around the exterior streets for free. Hoi An is one of Vietnam's most photogenic destinations - bring your camera. Avoid the expensive tourist restaurants along the main streets and head to the local market area for better prices.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (50,000-80,000 VND/day) and cycle 4km to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach - both free to access. Enjoy the beautiful beach in the morning before it gets too hot. Swim and relax. The cycling route through rice paddies and villages is scenic and very enjoyable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hoi An and visit the Hoi An Museum of Folk Culture (free or small fee) and the Museum of Trading Ceramics (120,000 VND included in Ancient Town ticket). Explore the covered market for fresh produce, local snacks, and cheap souvenirs. Visit a local tailor shop to see traditional Vietnamese textile craftsmanship (custom clothes are affordable but takes 24-48 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Join a budget cooking class (from 200,000-350,000 VND) to learn how to make Vietnamese dishes - many include a market tour. Alternatively, take a free lantern-making class offered by some guesthouses. End the evening with a walk through the lantern-lit Ancient Town.

meals.breakfast: Mi Quang (Quang Nam turmeric noodles) at a local breakfast stall - 35,000-50,000 VND
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at the beach shacks on An Bang Beach - grilled fish or seafood noodles for 80,000-120,000 VND
meals.dinner: Banh Mi Phuong (Hoi An's most famous banh mi shop, featured by Anthony Bourdain) - 35,000-45,000 VND. Add some Banh Xeo (sizzling pancakes) from a street stall for 40,000-60,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Banh Mi Phuong is located at 2B Phan Chau Trinh Street and is legendary among backpackers - expect a short queue. The bicycle ride to the beach is a highlight of any Hoi An visit. If you want custom clothing made, order today so it's ready before you leave. Budget tip: eat at the covered market's food stalls for the cheapest and most authentic Hoi An meals.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 - April 23, 2027 (Travel to Ho Chi Minh City)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Hoi An guesthouse. Take a shuttle to Da Nang Airport (50,000-100,000 VND) for a budget flight to Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC/Saigon). Budget airlines like VietJet Air or Bamboo Airways offer flights from 300,000-600,000 VND if booked in advance. Alternatively, take the overnight train for a more budget-friendly option. Arrive in HCMC and take bus No. 152 from the airport to the city center (20,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a budget hostel in the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district (dorm beds from 100,000-150,000 VND). Explore the buzzing Pham Ngu Lao area - the heart of budget travel in HCMC. Visit the nearby Ben Thanh Market (free entry) to browse local goods, food, and souvenirs. Bargain hard!
day_by_day.evening: Explore the streets around Bui Vien Walking Street - HCMC's famous backpacker street that comes alive at night with food stalls, bars, and street performers. Sample street food and enjoy the electric atmosphere of Saigon's nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Quick Banh Mi or coffee at a local cafe before heading to the airport - 30,000-50,000 VND
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork) - HCMC's iconic dish - at a local stall in the Pham Ngu Lao area - 40,000-60,000 VND
meals.dinner: Street food crawl on Bui Vien Street: Banh Trang Nuong (Vietnamese pizza), grilled skewers, and fresh coconut - 80,000-120,000 VND total

day_by_day.notes: Book your flight from Da Nang to HCMC well in advance for the best budget fares. The Pham Ngu Lao area is the classic backpacker hub with the cheapest accommodation, food, and tour options in HCMC. Be aware of motorbike bag snatchers in HCMC - keep bags on the inside away from the road. The city is best explored by grab bike for short distances.

day_by_day.date: Day 10 - April 24, 2027 (Ho Chi Minh City Highlights)
day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Remnants Museum (40,000 VND) - one of the most powerful and important museums in Southeast Asia, documenting the Vietnam War from the Vietnamese perspective. Allow 2 hours. Afterward, walk to the Reunification Palace (40,000 VND) - the former presidential palace where the Vietnam War officially ended on April 30, 1975.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Notre-Dame Cathedral (free, exterior) and the historic Central Post Office designed by Gustave Eiffel (free entry, still functioning). Walk through the French colonial district. Head to the Saigon River waterfront for views of the city. Visit Cho Lon (Chinatown) via local bus - explore Binh Tay Market and the colorful Thien Hau Temple (free).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Pham Ngu Lao for your final evening in Vietnam. Visit the vibrant night food market. Reflect on your journey over a final Vietnamese meal and a cold Saigon beer. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at the night market stalls. Pack up and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Hu Tieu Nam Vang (Phnom Penh-style noodle soup) - a HCMC breakfast staple - at a local stall - 40,000-60,000 VND
meals.lunch: Banh Mi Op La (Vietnamese egg banh mi) or Com Tam at a local restaurant in Chinatown - 35,000-55,000 VND
meals.dinner: Final Vietnamese feast: Lau (hot pot) at a budget local restaurant on Pham Ngu Lao - 100,000-150,000 VND per person, or a street food spread of your Vietnam favorites

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum is emotionally intense - allow time to process what you see. HCMC moves at a frantic pace compared to Hanoi - be cautious when crossing streets (walk slowly and steadily, traffic will flow around you). For your departure, grab bus No. 152 back to Tan Son Nhat Airport for just 20,000 VND. Total 10-day trip budget estimate: approximately 3,000,000-4,500,000 VND (~$120-180 USD) excluding flights and accommodation.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to boutique hotel in the Old Quarter (approximately 45 minutes by taxi or Grab app, ~200,000 VND). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely self-guided walk through the 36 Streets of the Old Quarter. Explore the narrow lanes, browse local craft shops, and soak in the atmosphere. Visit Hoan Kiem Lake and the iconic red Huc Bridge leading to Ngoc Son Temple (entrance ~30,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Hanoi Weekend Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Thu–Sun). Watch street performers, browse handicrafts, and ease into Vietnamese culture. Enjoy the buzzing Old Quarter nightlife from a street-side plastic stool.

meals.breakfast: N/A — mid-flight or airport
meals.lunch: Grab a bowl of Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodles) at a local Old Quarter stall near Hang Dieu Street (~50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bun Cha Huong Lien (the 'Obama Bun Cha' restaurant) on Le Van Huu Street — try the iconic grilled pork with rice noodles (~80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Use Grab (Vietnam's Uber) for reliable and affordable transport from the airport. Exchange currency at the airport or use an ATM in the Old Quarter. Keep small bills handy for street food.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Vietnamese breakfast, then visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex (open mornings only, closed Mon & Fri). See the Presidential Palace, Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, and the One Pillar Pagoda. Arrive early to avoid queues (~40,000 VND combined entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (taxi ~15 min, entry ~40,000 VND) — one of Southeast Asia's best cultural museums showcasing 54 ethnic groups. Spend 2–3 hours exploring indoor and outdoor exhibits. Return to the Old Quarter via Grab.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free Hoan Kiem Lake evening walk — locals practice tai chi, badminton, and aerobics around the lake. Explore Ta Hien Street ('Beer Street') for a cold Bia Hoi (fresh draft beer, ~10,000–15,000 VND per glass) and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef pho) at Pho Gia Truyen on Bat Dan Street — a legendary Old Quarter institution (~60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Banh Mi from a street cart near the museum area (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong on Cha Ca Street — try the famous turmeric-marinated fish with dill, a Hanoi specialty (~150,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum requires modest dress (shoulders and knees covered). Photography inside the mausoleum is strictly prohibited. Arrive before 10:30 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ninh Binh (2.5 hours by bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat station, ~100,000 VND). Visit Trang An Landscape Complex — take a 2-hour boat tour through limestone karsts, caves, and rice paddies (entry + boat ~250,000 VND). Often called 'Halong Bay on land.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) and cycle to Bich Dong Pagoda, a stunning cave pagoda carved into a limestone cliff. Then ride through Tam Coc village's scenic countryside. Optional: climb to Hang Mua viewpoint for panoramic valley views (~100,000 VND entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by late afternoon bus. Freshen up at the hotel. Spend the evening exploring Hang Buom and Hang Ngang streets for souvenir shopping and local snacks.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Xeo (sticky rice with mung bean) from a street vendor near the hotel (~30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Rang (fried rice) or grilled goat meat (de nuong) — Ninh Binh's local specialty at a riverside restaurant (~80,000–120,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) at Banh Cuon Gia Truyen on Thanh Nien Road (~50,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ninh Binh bus ticket the day before at the hotel or via the 12Go Asia app. Bring sunscreen and a hat — the boat tour is mostly outdoors. Wear comfortable shoes for Hang Mua climb (500 stone steps).

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hanoi for Hoi An by overnight train or morning flight. Recommended: take the 7:00 AM Vietjet/Bamboo Airways flight to Da Nang (~800,000–1,200,000 VND booked in advance). Arrive Da Nang ~8:30 AM, then transfer to Hoi An by taxi (45 min, ~300,000 VND shared or ~400,000 VND private).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a mid-range guesthouse in Hoi An Ancient Town. Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town on foot: visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge, Phuc Kien Assembly Hall, and browse the lantern-lit streets. Pick up a tailoring quote if interested (Hoi An is famous for custom clothing).
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Hoi An Night Market on An Hoi Island (cross the footbridge from the Ancient Town). Browse handmade lanterns, local art, and street food stalls. Watch the lanterns float on the Thu Bon River.

meals.breakfast: Airport or in-flight snack
meals.lunch: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish) at Thanh Cao Lau on Thai Phien Street (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) and fried wontons at White Rose Restaurant on Hai Ba Trung Street (~80,000–120,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An Ancient Town charges an entry fee of ~120,000 VND which covers 5 heritage site tickets. Buy at the ticket booths near the entrance. Hoi An is best explored on foot or by bicycle.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~60,000 VND/day) and cycle 4 km to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach. Enjoy a relaxed morning swim in the South China Sea. The beaches are quieter in the morning and offer beautiful views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and join a half-day Hoi An cooking class (many options available, ~400,000–600,000 VND including market visit). Learn to make Banh Xeo (sizzling pancakes), fresh spring rolls, and a local soup. Classes typically include a trip to the central market.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Ancient Town by night when it glows with hundreds of silk lanterns. Release a floating lantern on the Thu Bon River (~20,000–30,000 VND). Browse the tailors if you placed an order — fittings often happen in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong on Phan Chau Trinh Street — Anthony Bourdain's favorite Banh Mi in Vietnam (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Included in cooking class
meals.dinner: Mi Quang (turmeric noodles with shrimp and pork) at a local restaurant on Truong Minh Luong Street (~60,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class the day before at your guesthouse or directly at a school like Red Bridge or Morning Glory. April weather in Hoi An is warm and mostly dry — ideal beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to My Son Sanctuary (30 km from Hoi An, shared minibus tour ~150,000–200,000 VND). Explore the ancient Cham Hindu temple complex dating back to the 4th century, set in a jungle valley. Entry ~150,000 VND.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hoi An by early afternoon. Visit the Hoi An Museum of History and Culture or the Museum of Trading Ceramics in the Ancient Town (covered by the heritage ticket). Pick up any tailored clothing orders.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar overlooking the Thu Bon River. Then take an evening cyclo (pedicab) ride through the Ancient Town (~80,000–100,000 VND for 30 minutes) for a unique perspective.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Man (savory sticky rice) from a street cart near the hotel (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for My Son or eat at the on-site canteen (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at a restaurant along Bach Dang Street overlooking the river (~150,000–200,000 VND for fresh grilled fish and prawns)

day_by_day.notes: My Son is best visited early morning to avoid heat — the shared tour usually departs at 8:00 AM. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring insect repellent for the jungle setting.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hoi An for Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC/Saigon). Take a taxi to Da Nang airport (~400,000 VND) and fly to Tan Son Nhat International Airport (~900,000–1,300,000 VND). Arrive mid-morning. Transfer to your hotel in District 1 or the Backpacker District (Pham Ngu Lao area) by Grab (~150,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district — grab a map and walk to the War Remnants Museum on Vo Van Tan Street (entry ~40,000 VND). This powerful museum documents the Vietnam War through photographs and artifacts. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Ben Thanh Market area for the Ben Thanh Night Market (open from 6 PM). Browse street food stalls, local fashion, and souvenirs. The surrounding streets buzz with energy after dark.

meals.breakfast: Airport coffee and pastry
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork) at Com Tam Moc on Nguyen Trai Street — a HCMC staple (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food feast at the Ben Thanh Night Market — try Banh Trang Nuong (Vietnamese pizza), fresh spring rolls, and sugar cane juice (~100,000–150,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: HCMC traffic is intense — use Grab for all rides and be cautious when crossing streets (cross slowly and steadily, traffic flows around you). Keep your belongings secure in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reunification Palace (formerly Independence Palace) — a fascinating time capsule of 1970s Vietnamese government architecture (entry ~40,000 VND). Then walk to the nearby Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon and the Central Post Office, both beautiful French colonial landmarks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a Grab to District 4 for a street food walking tour on your own — District 4 is known as HCMC's most authentic food district. Try Bun Mam (fermented fish noodle soup), Goi Cuon (fresh spring rolls), and Che (sweet dessert soups). Then visit the Fine Arts Museum on Pho Duc Chinh Street (~30,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Bui Vien Street ('Walking Street') in the backpacker district for HCMC's famous nightlife. Enjoy live music, neon lights, and the electric atmosphere. Alternatively, take a sunset cruise on the Saigon River (~200,000–300,000 VND for a 1-hour cruise).

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from a street cart on De Tham Street (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Hu Tieu Nam Vang (Phnom Penh-style noodle soup) at a District 4 street stall (~60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Pho Hung on Nguyen Trai Street for a classic bowl of southern-style pho (~70,000–90,000 VND), then dessert at a Che cart

day_by_day.notes: The Reunification Palace opens at 7:30 AM — arrive early to explore before tour groups arrive. Consider hiring an audio guide (~30,000 VND extra) for full historical context.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (40 km northwest of HCMC). Join a half-day group tour departing at 8:00 AM (~250,000–350,000 VND including transport and entry). Crawl through the narrow wartime tunnels, see booby traps, and learn about Viet Cong guerrilla warfare. Return to HCMC by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Jade Emperor Pagoda (Phuoc Hai Tu) on Mai Thi Luu Street — one of HCMC's most atmospheric temples, filled with incense smoke and intricate Taoist and Buddhist iconography. Free entry. Then explore the surrounding Tan Dinh neighborhood and its pink Tan Dinh Church.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on dinner at a rooftop restaurant in District 1 for skyline views — try Chill Skybar or a mid-range rooftop eatery on Nguyen Hue Walking Street. End the evening with a walk along Nguyen Hue Boulevard, HCMC's grand pedestrian promenade.

meals.breakfast: Chao (Vietnamese rice porridge) with century egg at a local pho shop (~40,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Banh Xeo (sizzling crepe) at Banh Xeo 46A on Dinh Cong Trang Street (~100,000–130,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Rooftop dining at a mid-range restaurant on Nguyen Hue — budget ~200,000–300,000 VND for Vietnamese fusion dishes and a drink

day_by_day.notes: Book the Cu Chi Tunnels tour the night before through your hotel or a reputable agency like Sinh Tourist. Wear old clothes you don't mind getting dusty. The tunnels are claustrophobic — those with anxiety may prefer the wider 'tourist tunnels' option.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Vietnam — visit the Binh Tay Market in Cholon (Chinatown District 5, ~20 min by Grab). This wholesale market is more authentic and less touristy than Ben Thanh. Explore the vibrant Chinese-Vietnamese neighborhood, visit the Thien Hau Pagoda dedicated to the Goddess of the Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to District 1 for last-minute souvenir shopping on Dong Khoi Street or at the Ben Thanh Market. Pick up Vietnamese coffee (ca phe), lacquerware, silk scarves, or handmade crafts. Pack and prepare for departure. Head to Tan Son Nhat Airport allowing 2.5–3 hours before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Ho Chi Minh City. Reflect on 10 incredible days across Vietnam's north, center, and south.

meals.breakfast: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls with pork) at a local stall near the hotel (~50,000 VND) — a perfect final Vietnamese breakfast
meals.lunch: Dim Sum or Hu Tieu in Cholon's Chinatown (~80,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or a quick Pho at a terminal restaurant (~100,000–150,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for Cholon traffic when heading to the airport. Grab is reliable but can surge during peak hours (5–7 PM). Keep some VND for airport purchases — exchange remaining dong back to your currency at the airport or spend it on last-minute snacks and coffee.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to Boutique Stay in the Old Quarter, Hanoi (approximately 45 minutes). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your boutique hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the 36 Streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter. Explore the narrow, atmospheric lanes named after their historic trades — Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and Hang Ma (Paper Votive Street). Visit Ngoc Son Temple on Hoan Kiem Lake for a tranquil introduction to Vietnamese spirituality and architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the illuminated Hoan Kiem Lake promenade as the city comes alive. Experience the famous Hanoi Old Quarter Night Market on Hang Dao Street — browse silk scarves, lacquerware, and handcrafted souvenirs. Wind down with a signature cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the Old Quarter skyline.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge)
meals.lunch: Light welcome meal at the hotel's in-house restaurant or a nearby premium café such as Cong Caphe — Vietnamese iced coconut coffee and bánh mì with premium fillings
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cha Ca Thang Long, a legendary Old Quarter institution famous for the iconic Hanoi dish Chả Cá Lã Vọng — turmeric-marinated grilled fish with dill, served tableside on a sizzling pan

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Allow time for jet lag recovery. Confirm hotel concierge assistance for the next 9 days of experiences and private transfers.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Hoan Kiem District cultural highlights — begin with the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu), Vietnam's first national university built in 1070, followed by the Fine Arts Museum of Vietnam showcasing lacquer paintings, silk art, and bronze sculptures spanning centuries of Vietnamese artistic heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive premium street food walking tour of the Old Quarter led by a local culinary expert. Sample Hanoi's most celebrated dishes at their authentic sources: Phở Bò (beef noodle soup) at a decades-old family stall, Bún Chả (grilled pork with rice noodles), Bánh Cuốn (steamed rice rolls), and Nem Rán (crispy spring rolls). Visit a traditional Vietnamese tea house for a ceremonial tasting.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a water puppet show at the Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre — a UNESCO-recognized art form unique to northern Vietnam, accompanied by live traditional music. Post-show dinner at a premium restaurant in the Old Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Lavish breakfast at the boutique hotel — Vietnamese-style spread with Xôi (sticky rice), Bánh Mì, tropical fruits, and Vietnamese drip coffee
meals.lunch: Street food tour includes tastings across 6–8 vendors — effectively a full curated lunch experience
meals.dinner: Dinner at Maison Vie or a comparable fine-dining Vietnamese restaurant — tasting menu featuring elevated northern Vietnamese cuisine with premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre in advance as performances sell out quickly. The street food tour is best enjoyed on an empty stomach — skip heavy snacking before.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Hoa Lo Prison Museum (the 'Hanoi Hilton') for a sobering and deeply educational cultural experience. Afterward, explore the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex — the Presidential Palace, Ho Chi Minh's stilt house, and the tranquil One Pillar Pagoda (Chùa Một Cột), one of Vietnam's most iconic structures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cyclo (traditional rickshaw) tour through the Old Quarter's labyrinthine backstreets, visiting hidden courtyards, family-run workshops producing traditional crafts, and a French colonial architectural trail along Trang Tien and Ngo Quyen streets. Stop at the St. Joseph's Cathedral for photographs and quiet reflection.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class experience at a premium culinary school in the Old Quarter — learn to prepare three classic Hanoian dishes including Phở broth from scratch, fresh spring rolls, and a traditional dessert. Enjoy your creations as dinner with the class group.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — Cháo (Vietnamese rice porridge) with century egg and ginger, fresh baguette with pâté, and Vietnamese coffee
meals.lunch: Bún Bò Nam Bộ (southern-style beef noodle salad) at a well-regarded Old Quarter lunch spot recommended by the hotel concierge
meals.dinner: Dishes prepared during the evening cooking class, served with local craft beer or Vietnamese wine

day_by_day.notes: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays and has strict dress code requirements (covered shoulders and knees). Confirm opening hours with the concierge the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hanoi by private luxury transfer (approximately 3.5 hours) to Ha Long Bay. En route, stop at a traditional lacquerware workshop in the outskirts of Hanoi for a behind-the-scenes tour of this centuries-old Vietnamese craft. Board your premium overnight junk cruise at Ha Long Bay Marina — welcome champagne and orientation briefing on deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cruise through the UNESCO World Heritage limestone karst landscape of Ha Long Bay. Visit Sung Sot Cave (Surprise Cave) — one of the bay's largest and most spectacular grottos with dramatic illuminated stalactites and stalagmites. Kayaking excursion through hidden lagoons and floating fishing villages.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the cruise deck with panoramic views of the karst towers reflected in the emerald water. Multi-course seafood dinner on board — fresh squid, prawns, and clams caught the same day, prepared by the onboard chef. Squid fishing activity off the boat deck under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel before departure — full Vietnamese and international buffet
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch on board the cruise — Vietnamese spring rolls, fresh seafood, and tropical fruits served as the boat departs into the bay
meals.dinner: Premium 5-course seafood dinner on the junk cruise deck — steamed lobster, grilled scallops with butter and garlic, fish in ginger sauce, and Vietnamese desserts

day_by_day.notes: Pack light for the overnight cruise — a small overnight bag is recommended. The premium cruise includes all meals, kayaking, and cave visits. Confirm cruise booking at least 2 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Tai Chi session on the sundeck at sunrise over Ha Long Bay — a serene and unforgettable experience. After breakfast, a final kayaking session or bamboo boat ride through a secluded lagoon. Disembark and private transfer back to Hanoi, then onward to Noi Bai Airport for a domestic flight to Da Nang (approximately 1.5 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Da Nang and private transfer to Hoi An Ancient Town (approximately 30 minutes). Check into a luxury boutique resort in or near Hoi An's ancient town. After settling in, take a leisurely first walk through the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town — the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge, the colorful lantern-lit streets, and the historic merchant houses.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the magical Hoi An Ancient Town by night — the town glows with hundreds of silk lanterns reflected in the Thu Bon River. Take a boat ride on the river with floating lanterns for good luck. Dinner at a premium Hoi An restaurant on the riverfront.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast on the Ha Long Bay cruise before disembarkation
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Da Nang airport or during transfer — Mì Quảng (turmeric noodles with pork and shrimp) at a recommended local spot near the airport
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Field Restaurant or Mango Mango in Hoi An — refined Vietnamese cuisine in an elegant garden or riverside setting, featuring Hoi An specialties like Cao Lầu noodles and White Rose dumplings

day_by_day.notes: The domestic flight from Hanoi to Da Nang should be pre-booked. Hoi An Ancient Town is best explored on foot or by bicycle — the resort concierge can arrange bicycle rentals for the following days.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided cultural tour of Hoi An Ancient Town — visit the 200-year-old Tan Ky Merchant House, the Phuc Kien Fujian Chinese Assembly Hall with its stunning altar and courtyard, and the Japanese Covered Bridge. Attend a traditional lantern-making workshop with a local artisan family and craft your own silk lantern to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Motorbike or bicycle ride through the lush countryside surrounding Hoi An — visit rice paddies, vegetable farming villages, and a traditional boat-building workshop on the Thu Bon River. Stop at the Tra Que Vegetable Village, where local farmers grow organic herbs and vegetables using centuries-old methods. Join a farm-to-table cooking demonstration.
day_by_day.evening: Premium street food tour of Hoi An's famous Night Market and surrounding alleyways — taste Bánh Mì Phượng (the most celebrated bánh mì in Vietnam, made famous globally by Anthony Bourdain), Cao Lầu noodles, Bánh Xèo (sizzling Vietnamese crepes), and fresh coconut ice cream. End the evening with a cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the ancient town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — Vietnamese Phở, fresh tropical fruit platter, eggs to order, and Vietnamese iced coffee
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch at Tra Que Village — freshly harvested herb salads, steamed rice, and grilled fish cooked by the farming family
meals.dinner: Street food tour dinner across multiple vendors in the Hoi An Night Market area — budget approximately 300,000–500,000 VND per person for a comprehensive tasting

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An's Ancient Town has vehicle restrictions — the inner core is pedestrian-only during certain hours. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Bánh Mì Phượng stall often has queues — visit before 18:30 for shorter waits.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Marble Mountains (Ngũ Hành Sơn) near Da Nang — a cluster of five marble and limestone hills with Buddhist sanctuaries, caves, and pagodas built into the rock face. Climb to the summit for panoramic views of Da Nang's coastline and the South China Sea. Visit the Am Phu Cave (Hell Cave) and Huyen Khong Cave with its natural skylight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the My Son Sanctuary — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the most significant Hindu temple complex in Southeast Asia, built by the ancient Cham civilization between the 4th and 14th centuries. Private guided tour with an expert archaeologist or historian for an in-depth cultural immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hoi An for a relaxing evening. Optional: traditional Vietnamese massage and spa treatment at the resort (90-minute session). Dinner at a premium restaurant in the ancient town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — full spread with Xôi Gà (sticky rice with chicken), fresh pastries, and fruit
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the resort, enjoyed at the My Son Sanctuary grounds
meals.dinner: Dinner at Morning Glory Restaurant in Hoi An — a beloved institution run by celebrated chef Trinh Diem Vy, serving refined Hoi An and Central Vietnamese cuisine

day_by_day.notes: My Son Sanctuary is most atmospheric in the late afternoon light. Bring insect repellent and sun protection — the site is largely open-air. The drive from Hoi An to My Son is approximately 45 minutes each way.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Hoi An to Da Nang Airport (30 minutes) for a domestic flight to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Upon arrival, private luxury transfer to a premium boutique hotel in District 1, the vibrant heart of Saigon. Check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive cultural afternoon in Saigon's historic District 1 — visit the Reunification Palace (Dinh Thong Nhat), where the Vietnam War officially ended on April 30, 1975, followed by the War Remnants Museum for a powerful and sobering historical perspective. Walk to the stunning Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon and the French colonial Central Post Office, designed by Gustave Eiffel.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Saigon's legendary street food scene on a premium food tour by motorbike through the city's most authentic neighborhoods — District 1, District 3, and District 5 (Cholon, Saigon's Chinatown). Taste Hủ Tiếu (southern pork noodle soup), Bánh Tráng Nướng (grilled rice paper pizza), Bò Bía (fresh Vietnamese spring rolls), and chè (sweet dessert soups).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Hoi An resort before departure
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at a rooftop restaurant in District 1 after hotel check-in — Cơm Tấm (broken rice with grilled pork chop) elevated to fine-dining standard at a renowned Saigon establishment
meals.dinner: Motorbike street food tour dinner across 6–8 stops through Saigon's most vibrant food districts

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum contains graphic imagery — be prepared for an emotionally intense experience. The motorbike food tour requires a waiver; helmets are provided. Confirm the tour with the hotel concierge upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Cu Chi Tunnels — the extraordinary 250km underground network used by Viet Cong guerrillas during the Vietnam War. Private guided tour with a historian for deep context. Crawl through original tunnel sections, see booby trap demonstrations, and visit a firing range. Return to Saigon by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Saigon's thriving arts and culture scene — visit the Museum of Vietnamese History in the Botanic Gardens, then wander through the creative hub of the Saigon Artistic Collective or a contemporary Vietnamese gallery in District 3. Stroll through the Ben Thanh Market area for premium Vietnamese handicrafts, silk, and ao dai (traditional dress) — consider having a custom ao dai tailored (same-day express service available at select boutiques).
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop cocktails at the Saigon Skydeck or a premium rooftop bar in District 1 with panoramic city views as the sun sets over Saigon. Farewell dinner at a world-class Vietnamese fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — full Vietnamese and international buffet with Phở, Bánh Mì, tropical fruits, and freshly brewed Vietnamese coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside restaurant near the Cu Chi Tunnels — traditional southern Vietnamese dishes including Cá Kho Tộ (caramelized fish in clay pot) and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Nhà Hàng Ngon (Restaurant Ngon) or Quince Saigon — a curated tasting menu of Vietnamese cuisine from all three regions (North, Central, South) paired with premium Vietnamese wines or cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Cu Chi Tunnels excursion departs early (recommend 07:30) to beat the heat and crowds. The tunnels are narrow and low — those with claustrophobia should notify the guide in advance. Ben Thanh Market closes around 18:00.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Saigon — leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Last-minute exploration of the Dong Khoi Street luxury boutique corridor for premium Vietnamese silk, lacquerware, and coffee souvenirs. Visit Saigon's iconic Continental Hotel for a historical coffee on the terrace — immortalized in Graham Greene's 'The Quiet American.' Stroll along the Saigon River promenade for final city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Tan Son Nhat International Airport for departure. Allow 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and immigration. Enjoy the airport lounge with complimentary refreshments before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Ho Chi Minh City — carry the memories of 10 extraordinary days across Vietnam's most iconic destinations.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at the hotel — signature Vietnamese spread with Cháo, Bánh Mì, fresh fruit, and the finest Vietnamese drip coffee as a farewell ritual
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a premium café on Dong Khoi Street — Vietnamese iced coffee, fresh spring rolls, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Pack any purchased lacquerware, ceramics, or fragile items carefully. Note that Vietnamese coffee, dried spices, and packaged foods are generally permitted in checked luggage. Keep ao dai and silk items in carry-on to avoid damage. Confirm departure terminal with the hotel concierge the evening before.
